question: Should ClickClack own a built-in multi-format artifact rendering boundary in the core web client?
rationale: The implementation is technically strong, but it creates lasting dependency, parser, sandbox, and hostile-input testing obligations beyond current attachment-card behavior.

options.title: Accept the bounded core viewer
options.body: Adopt the strict read-only renderer and maintain its resource limits, isolation guarantees, and browser security suite as a core feature.

options.title: Exclude uploaded HTML
options.body: Land code, text, Markdown, and PDF support while keeping arbitrary HTML download-only to reduce the permanent security surface.

options.title: Retain download cards
options.body: Decline the viewer if ClickClack should not own client-side parsing of untrusted artifact formats.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded core viewer
recommendation.body: Adopt the strict read-only renderer and maintain its resource limits, isolation guarantees, and browser security suite as a core feature.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the adjacent current-main behavior and owns the latest integration and security-hardening history for this PR.
